posts.headline: His affordable machines have helped *10,000+ people in Mizoram*
posts.body: Lalbiakzuala Ralte builds affordable machines for hill farmers and artisans. On 25 Nov, he won the Jamnalal Bajaj Award and ₹20 lakh in Mumbai.
posts.caption:
He builds simple machines for the hills of Mizoram 🛠️

Lalbiakzuala Ralte makes affordable machines for farmers, artisans and young people in Mizoram's hilly terrain: a portable bamboo incense-stick machine, a noodle maker, a fodder grinder, an arecanut cleaning and husking machine, and ropeways that carry produce down from hillside farms. His work has benefited more than 10,000 people.

On 25 November in Mumbai, he received the Jamnalal Bajaj Award for Application of Science and Technology for Rural Development, with ₹20 lakh, a citation and a trophy. 🏆

Sources: EastMojo, ThePrint (PTI)

posts.headline: 5,000 youth trained. *71% were women*
posts.sub: Samsung trained and certified 5,000 young people in Tamil Nadu in AI, coding, big data and IoT in 2025.

slides.title: Three paths to *future-ready skills*
slides.body: Samsung Innovation Campus (AI, coding, IoT), Solve for Tomorrow (tech ideas for local problems) and Samsung DOST (retail and repair skills).

slides.title: 6 Tamil Nadu teams in India's *Top 40*
slides.body: 5,000+ Tamil Nadu students have joined Solve for Tomorrow. One Chennai team is building a pad that turns text and images into Braille.

slides.title: Learning on the job
slides.body: Via Samsung DOST in Tamil Nadu. About 500 more are in on-the-job training now.

posts.takeaway: Skills open doors to good work. *5,000 more in AI next.*
posts.source: Samsung Newsroom India (23 Nov 2026), India CSR (25 Nov 2026)
posts.caption:
5,000 young people trained. 71% were women. 💻✨

Samsung India's social-good programmes are helping Tamil Nadu's youth build skills for the future. In 2025, Samsung Innovation Campus trained and certified 5,000 young people in the state in AI, coding, big data and IoT, and 71% of them were women.

Through Solve for Tomorrow, 5,000+ Tamil Nadu students have taken on local problems with technology, and 6 teams from the state reached the national Top 40 this year. Samsung DOST has trained about 1,700 young people for retail and service jobs, with about 500 more in on-the-job training now. 🙌

"Access to information should never be a barrier," says Vishwa Kumaresh of Team TouchPad, Chennai, who is building a tactile pad that turns images and text into Braille.

Sources: Samsung Newsroom India, India CSR

posts.stat_label: million tonnes of foodgrain grown in 2025-26, India's highest ever (final estimates)
posts.headline: Thank you, farmers: *a record harvest*
points: Maize jumped about 27% to 55.03 Mt; rice reached 155.15 Mt
Wheat: 122.06 Mt. Pulses: up 6.1% to 27.24 Mt
posts.source: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare final estimates (26 Nov 2026) via DD India, Daily Excelsior, ETV Bharat
posts.caption:
India just grew its biggest harvest ever 🌾

Foodgrain production in 2025-26 reached a record 378.5 million tonnes, according to the Agriculture Ministry's final estimates released on 26 November. That's 20.8 million tonnes (about 5.8%) more than in 2024-25.

🌽 Maize jumped about 27% to 55.03 million tonnes
🍚 Rice reached 155.15 million tonnes
🌾 Wheat reached 122.06 million tonnes
🫘 Pulses rose 6.1% to 27.24 million tonnes

Behind every number are millions of farming families. Thank you! 🙏

Sources: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare data via DD India, Daily Excelsior, ETV Bharat

posts.headline: 1,000 women farmers. Their rice yield is *up about 58%*
posts.sub: How women in 25 villages of Sindhudurg, Maharashtra, switched to a new way of growing rice.

slides.title: Erratic rain, *rising costs*
slides.body: Small farmers on the Konkan coast faced erratic monsoons, costly labour and pricier fertiliser. Old methods kept fields flooded.

slides.title: Women worked each other's fields
slides.body: Instead of hiring labour, they farmed as a group and planned on WhatsApp. Fields stayed moist, not flooded.

slides.title: From 34.9 kg to *55.2 kg per 100 m²*. About 58% more rice.
slides.body: One seedling grew 20-25 shoots, vs 6-12 the old way. The group also farmed 8 more hectares.

posts.takeaway: "We women handle the manual work in rice farming." When women lead the field, *harvests grow*.
posts.source: UNDP India (11 Nov 2026), The Logical Indian (25 Nov 2026)
posts.caption:
1,000 women farmers. Rice yields up about 58%. 🌾💪

In 25 villages of Sindhudurg on Maharashtra's Konkan coast, about 1,000 women farmers switched to SRI, a new way of growing rice, across 100 hectares. They planted a single young seedling 25 cm apart, kept fields moist instead of flooded, and worked in each other's fields instead of hiring labour.

The result: 55.2 kg of rice per 100 m², compared with 34.9 kg on traditional plots. Each plant grew 20-25 shoots from a single seedling. 🌱

"We women handle the manual work in rice farming," says Supriya Gawade of Streeshakti Mahila Gat, Talekarwadi. Now they are leading the change. 🙌

The work is part of the ECRICC project of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Maharashtra Forest Department, supported by the Green Climate Fund and UNDP India, and carried out in Sindhudurg by Dilasa Janvikas Pratishthan (@dilasasanstha).
